package_info.why_malicious: N/A – This report does not describe a malicious package. Instead, it analyzes the risks and attack surface associated with shadow and zombie APIs, and details how Checkmarx API Security helps identify and mitigate these risks. No actual malicious code or package is described in the report.

behavioral_signatures: Undocumented (shadow) API endpoints accessible in production environments, which are not present in official API documentation.
Deprecated (zombie) API versions or endpoints that remain reachable and can be accessed externally.
API endpoints lacking authentication or proper access controls, allowing unauthorized access.
Sensitive data exposure through undocumented or legacy API endpoints, potentially leaking confidential information.
file_indicators: Swagger/OpenAPI/RAML documentation files that do not match the actual implemented API endpoints in the codebase.
Presence of multiple versions of the same API within the codebase or deployment artifacts.
API endpoint definitions found in source code that are missing from official documentation files.
network_indicators: Unusual or unexpected API traffic directed to endpoints not listed in official API documentation.
External access attempts to legacy or deprecated API endpoints that should no longer be in use.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Correlate API documentation (Swagger, OpenAPI, RAML) with both source code and observed runtime traffic to identify undocumented (shadow) and deprecated (zombie) APIs. Scan source code repositories for API definitions that are not present in documentation. Monitor network traffic for requests to endpoints not covered by official API documentation. Use automated API discovery and inventory tools to detect discrepancies between code, documentation, and observed traffic, and flag any endpoints that are undocumented or deprecated for further review.
